profile.title: Precontemplative obesity nutrition assessment in a budget-constrained warehouse worker
profile.summary: This case teaches dietetics students to conduct a telehealth nutrition assessment with a precontemplative, financially-strained patient whose BMI of 30.1 kg/m2 and grazing/no-fixed-meal eating pattern mask underlying food insecurity and health-avoidance behaviors he is reluctant to disclose. The core teaching points are motivational interviewing with a resistant, pride-driven patient; eliciting an irregular grazing diet history and translating it into an assessable nutrition diagnosis; and recognizing a patient-vs-chart mismatch (he implies he is 'due' for a dental visit when the record shows his last cleaning was five years ago) as a cue to gently probe deferred self-care tied to household financial constraints."}
profile.setting: Telehealth video visit, patient at home in East Orange, NJ, sitting in his parked pickup truck in the driveway for quiet

patient.name: Brooks Little
patient.occupation: Part-time forklift operator at a regional warehouse distribution center
patient.appearance: Solidly built, weight carried mostly around the midsection, calling from the driver's seat of an older pickup truck parked outside his crowded house. Restless on camera - picks up objects, gestures a lot, leans in and out of frame while telling stories.

persona.personality: Proud, self-reliant, talkative and restless; covers insecurity with confidence, bravado, and long rambling stories. Doesn't like being told what to do and is quick to deflect anything that feels like a lecture, but softens when he feels respected rather than corrected.
persona.communicationStyle: Winding, anecdotal - starts answering a direct question and ends up telling a story about his truck's transmission or a coworker's drama. Hard to pin down to a straight answer. Uses plain, working-class language, no medical terms, and repeats things he's read on forums/YouTube as settled fact. Jokes to deflect when a topic (money, health gaps) gets close to home.
persona.emotionalState: Mildly annoyed and defensive about the visit being 'about a number,' underneath some quiet embarrassment he covers with humor and bluster
persona.background: Brooks is 43, works part-time as a forklift operator at a regional warehouse distribution center, and lives in East Orange, NJ in a crowded house of seven - him, his wife, three kids, and his in-laws. He's proud of his old pickup truck, which he fixes himself, and spends downtime watching DIY and conspiracy-adjacent YouTube channels. At work, guys call him 'Little' as a joke since he's actually the biggest guy on his shift, which he finds funny. He grew up working-class in East Orange where food was whatever stretched furthest, and that practical, no-frills attitude toward eating stuck with him - food is fuel to get through a long shift, not something to fuss over.
speechExamples: Man, you sound like my cousin who's into all that keto stuff - I read that's basically a scam too.
I don't really sit down to eat, I just grab whatever's around and keep moving.
Half the guys on my shift are bigger than me, so I don't know why this is such a big deal.
Dinner's whenever the house finally quiets down - could be ten, eleven at night, whenever.
I didn't come here for a lecture, doc - I mean, uh, whatever you are. No offense.
concerns: Doesn't want to be lectured or told what to do
Worried any 'diet thing' will cost money he doesn't have
Mildly annoyed that a number on a chart is driving the whole visit
Wants to stay strong enough to keep working his job
Would like to not get winded carrying furniture for his father-in-law
Wants people, especially his wife, to stop worrying about his weight

scenario.studentBrief: You are the dietetics student conducting a telehealth nutrition assessment with Brooks Little, a 43-year-old man referred after a BMI flag at his last physical. This is a first nutrition visit. Review his available chart information before the call, then conduct the video visit to complete a nutrition assessment and begin patient-centered counseling.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Referred for nutrition assessment due to BMI flag at last physical
scenario.openingLine: Yeah, hey - so my doctor's office said I had to do this nutrition call because of some number on my chart. I feel fine, honestly, not really sure what we're supposed to talk about.
tasks: Take a focused diet history, including meal pattern, typical foods/beverages, and timing of intake across a full day
Review available anthropometric and laboratory data and relate them to the nutrition assessment
Explore the patient's readiness to change and his personal goals using patient-centered interviewing techniques
Identify barriers to healthy eating, including any financial, household, or scheduling factors, without pressuring the patient to disclose more than he's comfortable with
Compare what the patient reports about his health/dental follow-up with what is documented in the record, and gently explore any discrepancy
Document a nutrition assessment note in ADIME format with an appropriate nutrition diagnosis and plan

facts.says: Sometimes I take an ibuprofen if my back's killing me after work.

facts.chart: No known drug or food allergies.
facts.says: No allergies that I know of, never had a reaction to anything.

facts.says: They checked my blood a while back, doc said everything looked normal.

facts.chart: No current fever, sore throat, or respiratory symptoms.
facts.says: I'm all better from that throat thing, no fever or nothing now.

facts.chart: Lives in a household of 7 (wife, three kids, in-laws) in East Orange, NJ
facts.says: It's me, my wife, our three kids, and her folks all under one roof. Place is never quiet, I'll tell you that.

facts.chart: Works part-time as a forklift operator at a regional warehouse distribution center, irregular shift hours
facts.says: I run a forklift part-time over at the warehouse. Hours bounce all over - sometimes nights, sometimes doubles.

facts.says: I'm on my feet all shift running that forklift. That's plenty of exercise, I don't need to be doing more at home.

facts.chart: Reports goal of being able to help father-in-law move furniture without getting winded
facts.says: I just want to not be gasping for air when I'm helping my wife's dad move furniture around.

facts.chart: States goal of staying strong enough to keep working his job
facts.says: Long as I can keep doing my job and not break down, that's all that matters to me.

facts.chart: States goal of not wanting his wife to worry about his health
facts.says: I don't want my wife up at night worrying about me, you know? That's the last thing I need.

facts.chart: Reports household has little day-to-day support for meal planning or cooking despite large size
facts.says: Seven people in that house and nobody's got time to sit down and plan a meal together. Everybody's doing their own thing.

facts.chart: Hints that household finances are tight some weeks, deflects when pressed
facts.says: Eh, some weeks it's tighter than others, you know how it is - hey, speaking of tight, you believe what they're charging for gas now?

facts.chart: Reports buying the cheapest food available per ounce regardless of nutritional content
facts.says: I'm the guy checking price per ounce in the aisle. Whatever stretches the furthest, that's what goes in the cart.

facts.chart: Admits sometimes skipping picking up an OTC item at the pharmacy to save money that week
facts.says: Sometimes I just skip grabbing something at the pharmacy that week if money's funny. It's not a big deal, I make do.

facts.chart: Reports he and his wife prioritize children's and in-laws' medical and dental needs over his own given limited household income
facts.says: Look, when it comes down to it, the kids and her folks get seen first. I'll get around to my own stuff eventually.

facts.chart: Reports recently switching to cheaper bulk chips and off-brand cold cuts as grocery budget tightened
facts.says: I started grabbing the bigger bag of the store-brand chips and the no-name cold cuts instead. Nobody's noticed, it's fine.

facts.chart: Reports embarrassment about not being able to prepare a full home-cooked meal for his family, masks it with humor
facts.says: Honestly? Kind of embarrassing, man, forty-three years old and I still can't throw together a real dinner for my own family. I just joke about being too busy so nobody asks.

facts.chart: Drinks a couple of beers on weekends with brothers-in-law, denies heavy drinking
facts.says: I'll have a couple beers with my brothers-in-law on the weekend, nothing crazy.

facts.chart: Reports fixing up an older pickup truck himself as a hobby, source of pride
facts.says: This truck right here, I've fixed up almost everything on it myself. That's my thing.

objectives.text: Apply motivational interviewing techniques to engage a patient in precontemplation who denies his weight is a problem, using his own stated goals as motivational levers rather than direct advice-giving
Elicit a detailed diet history from a patient with an irregular grazing pattern and translate scattered intake across a long day into an assessable eating pattern
Integrate anthropometric data and laboratory results into a nutrition assessment, distinguishing clinically relevant findings from normal/incidental results
Explore financial, household, and scheduling barriers to healthy eating in a patient who is reluctant to disclose economic strain, using sensitive, non-judgmental questioning
Identify a discrepancy between a patient's self-reported health follow-through and the documented record, and address it respectfully without shaming the patient
Document a complete nutrition assessment using the ADIME format, culminating in an appropriate nutrition diagnosis grounded in diet history, anthropometrics, labs, and psychosocial barriers

answerKey.primaryProblem: Excessive energy intake related to irregular grazing pattern, large late-night meal, and frequent sugar-sweetened beverage intake, as evidenced by BMI 30.1 kg/m2 (up from 29.3 kg/m2 two years ago), self-reported skipping of fixed meals, reliance on energy-dense convenience foods, and sweetened beverages as primary hydration source
differential: Excessive energy intake (grazing/snacking pattern, nutrition diagnosis)
Undesirable food choices (saturated fat/refined carbohydrate heavy pattern) contributing to elevated LDL
Limited access to healthy food/beverages related to financial resource constraints
Not ready for diet/lifestyle change (precontemplation stage) impacting readiness for nutrition intervention
keyFindings: BMI 30.1 kg/m2 (height 180 cm, weight 97.4 kg), up from BMI 29.3 kg/m2 (94.9 kg) in 2023 - a +2.5 kg gain over ~2 years
Total cholesterol 204.2 mg/dL (ref <200) and LDL 131.7 mg/dL (ref <100) mildly elevated; HDL 49.2 mg/dL and triglycerides 116.7 mg/dL both within normal range
No fixed meal schedule; grazes across a 14-16 hour day on chips, cold cuts, leftover rice, gas-station snacks, fried chicken, honey buns
Skips breakfast; relies on sugared coffee
One large meal late at night (10-11pm), often finishing children's leftover plates, frequently takes seconds
Hydration almost entirely sweet tea and soda; reports water 'doesn't fill him up'
Sedentary at home despite active forklift shifts; no structured exercise
Household of 7 on ~$16,700/year income, Medicaid-insured; buys cheapest food per unit cost
Reports being 'due' for a dental cleaning, implying a recent visit, but dental record shows last cleaning/exam was December 2020 - about five years prior
Precontemplation stage: minimizes BMI relevance, compares self favorably to coworkers, resists direct advice, distrusts dietitian guidance in favor of online sources
plan: Build rapport and use motivational interviewing (open-ended questions, reflective listening, affirmations) rather than direct advice-giving, given precontemplation stage
Elicit and document a 24-hour recall / typical day intake to quantify grazing pattern and late-night meal portions
Explore readiness to change using his own stated motivators (keeping up with work, not getting winded helping father-in-law, not worrying his wife) rather than imposing external goals
Gently explore financial barriers to food and healthcare access using non-judgmental, open-ended questions; validate without probing further if he deflects

Offer low-cost, low-effort swaps aligned with his existing routine if he shows any openness (e.g., unsweetened/lower-sugar beverage options, pairing a protein with existing snack choices) - framed as his choice, not prescription

Correct inaccurate nutrition beliefs (e.g., 'diets are a scam') gently and collaboratively, without directly contradicting him, offering evidence-based information as one more input alongside what he's read

Document ADIME note: Assessment (diet history, anthropometrics, labs, psychosocial/financial barriers), Diagnosis (excessive energy intake related to grazing pattern as evidenced by BMI 30.1 and dietary recall), Intervention (education/counseling offered, patient's response), Monitoring/Evaluation plan (follow-up visit, re-weigh, reassess readiness to change)
Recommend follow-up telehealth visit to reassess readiness and revisit any small changes attempted
Flag the dental care gap (last visit 2020) for the primary care team as a care-coordination note, without turning this visit into a dental lecture
redFlags: Weight trending upward over two years without a clear plateau or reversal
Mild dyslipidemia (elevated total cholesterol and LDL) that could progress without any lifestyle shift
Household food insecurity dynamics affecting both nutrition and healthcare utilization (skipping OTC pickups, deferring his own dental/medical care)
Low readiness to change combined with no support system for meal planning or cooking, increasing risk of continued or worsening weight trend
educationPoints: Explain BMI as one piece of a bigger picture (muscle mass, fat distribution, labs) rather than a single verdict, to reduce defensiveness
Normalize that eating patterns shaped by shift work and tight budgets are common and not a personal failing
Introduce the idea of 'swaps' rather than restriction - keeping familiar, affordable foods but adjusting frequency, portion, or pairing (e.g., protein with chips) to work within his existing routine

Clarify the difference between hydration needs and feeling full, and offer low-cost alternatives to sweetened beverages (e.g., unsweetened iced tea, infused water) without insisting he give up soda entirely
Briefly explain how a late, large meal plus limited daytime structure can affect how full/hungry he feels, inviting him to notice this rather than telling him it's wrong
Reinforce his autonomy and the fact that any changes are his choice, tying potential benefits directly to his stated goals (work stamina, keeping up with family, not worrying his wife)

mismatches.patientClaim: Brooks implies he's 'due' for a dental cleaning and hasn't been in just a few months, minimizing the gap when asked about dental follow-up
mismatches.recordEvidence: Dental exam, cleaning, and plaque/calculus removal performed 2020-12-10, with no dental visits documented since - a gap of about five years
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients may minimize gaps in self-care follow-through, especially when embarrassed; cross-checking visit history against patient report helps the clinician gently surface care-coordination needs without confrontation

mismatches.patientClaim: Brooks says his weight is basically unchanged and he hasn't noticed significant change recently, framing tighter pants as just getting older
mismatches.recordEvidence: Weight trend shows 94.9 kg on 2023-09-14 versus 97.4 kg on 2025-09-18, a 2.5 kg gain over about two years, corresponding to a BMI increase to 30.1 kg/m2
mismatches.teachingPoint: Patients in precontemplation may genuinely underperceive gradual weight change; comparing current anthropometrics to documented trend data provides objective evidence to anchor a non-judgmental conversation about the nutrition diagnosis
